title: Integrator loss leads to dsRNA formation that triggers the Integrated Stress Response
projectDescription: Integrator (INT) is a metazoan-specific complex that targets promoter-proximally paused RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) for termination, preventing immature RNAPII from entering gene bodies and functionally attenuating transcription of stress-responsive genes. Mutations in INT subunits are associated with many human diseases, including cancer, ciliopathies and neurodevelopmental disorders, but how reduced INT activity contributes to disease is unknown. Here, we demonstrate that loss of INT-mediated termination in human cells triggers the integrated stress response (ISR). INT-depletion causes upregulation of short genes such as the ISR transcription factor ATF3. Further, immature RNAPII that escapes into genes upon INT-depletion is prone to premature termination, generating incomplete pre-mRNAs with retained introns. Retroelements within retained introns form double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) that is recognized by Protein Kinase R (PKR), which drives ATF4 activation and prolonged ISR. Critically, patient cells with INT mutations exhibit dsRNA accumulation and ISR activation, thereby implicating chronic ISR in diseases caused by INT-deficiency.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Immunopurification: 10 million INTS1AID cells expressing near endogenous levels of HA- tagged SPT5 (+/- 500 µM auxin, 4h) were plated on 10 cm dishes the evening before harvesting. To collect lysates, media was aspirated, and plates were washed with room temperature 1x PBS. Cells were detached with pre-warmed trypsin and quenched with cold complete DMEM. Cells were then collected into 15 ml conical tubes on ice and spun down at 1000 rpm and 4°C for 4 mins. Supernatant was removed and pellets were resuspended in cold 1xPBS. Cell counts were taken, aiming for similar counts across conditions. Pellets were spun down again, supernatant removed and resuspended in 2ml cold complete lysis buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 100 mM sodium chloride, 10% glycerol, 1% NP40, 1mM MgCl2, 0.5 mM PMSF, and 0.5mM DTT). Next, to release the chromatin bound fraction, Benzonase (Sigma) treatment at 250U per ml lysate was performed. Samples were incubated at 4°C for 2 hrs with head over tail rotation. The lysate was then subjected to immunoprecipitation using anti-HA-agarose beads (Sigma). For beads preparation, 40 μl HA-agarose beads slurry was used per IP. Beads were washed 3 times with 1 ml cold IP wash buffer (20 mM HEPES pH 7.4, 100 mM potassium chloride, 10% glycerol, and 0.1% NP40). Lysates were then spun down at max speed and 4°C for 5 mins. 1% input material was taken for analysis by immunoblotting and the remaining lysate supernatant was transferred to washed HA-agarose beads and incubated at 4°C for 2 hours with rotation for immunoprecipitation. Beads were then washed 4 times with cold IP wash buffer followed by the fifth wash with cold 50 mM HEPES pH 7.4 while transferring to a fresh tube before elution. Digestion: Elutions from each sample was reduced with dithiothreitol to 2 mM, followed by incubation at 55°C for 60 minutes. Iodoacetamide was added to 10 mM and incubated in the dark at room temperature for 30 minutes to alkylate the proteins. Phosphoric acid was added to 1.2%, followed by six volumes of 90% methanol, 100 mM TEAB. The resulting solution was added to S-Trap micros (Protifi), and centrifuged at 4,000 x g for 1 minute. The S-Traps containing trapped protein were washed twice by centrifuging through 90% methanol, 100 mM TEAB. 1 ug of trypsin was brought up in 20 uL of 100 mM TEAB and added to the S-Trap, followed by an additional 20 µL of TEAB to ensure the sample did not dry out. The cap to the S-Trap was loosely screwed on but not tightened to ensure the solution was not pushed out of the S-Trap during digestion. Samples were placed in a humidity chamber at 37°C overnight. The next morning, the S-Trap was centrifuged at 4,000 x g for 1 minute to collect the digested peptides. Sequential additions of 0.1% TFA in acetonitrile and 0.1% TFA in 50% acetonitrile were added to the S-trap, centrifuged, and pooled. Samples were frozen and dried down in a Speed Vac (Labconco), then re-suspended in 0.1% trifluoroacetic acid prior to analysis. LC-MS/MS Analysis: Peptides were injected onto a 75 um x 2 cm trap column (Thermo Fisher) prior to re-focusing on an Aurora Elite 75 um x 15 cm C18 column (IonOpticks) using a Vanquish Neo UHPLC (Thermo Fisher), connected to an Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher).  Solvent A was 0.1% formic acid in water, while solvent B was 0.1% formic acid in 80% acetonitrile.  Ions were introduced to the mass spectrometer using an Easy-Spray source operating at 2 kV. The gradient began at 1% B and ramped to 5% B in 0.1 minutes, increased to 30% B in 12.1 minutes, increased to 40% in 0.7 minutes, and finally increased to 99% B in 0.1 minutes and was held for 2 minutes to wash the column for a total runtime of 15 minutes. After each run was completed, the column was re-equilibrated with 1% B prior to the next injection. The Orbitrap Astral was operated in data-independent acquisition (DIA) mode, with MS1 scans acquired in the Orbitrap at a resolution of 240,000, with a maximum injection time of 5 ms over a range of 380-980 m/z. DIA MS2 scans were acquired in the Astral mass analyzer with a 3 ms maximum injection time using 4 m/z windows from 380-980 m/z. The HCD collision energy was set to 25%, and the normalized AGC was set to 500%. Fragment ions were collected over a scan range of 150-2000 m/z. The cycle time was 0.6 seconds.
dataProcessingProtocol: The raw data were processed with DIA-NN version 1.8.1. For all experiments, data analysis was carried out using library-free analysis mode in DIA-NN. To annotate the library, the human UniProt ‘one protein sequence per gene’ database (UP000005640_9606, downloaded 4/7/2021) was used with ‘deep learning-based spectra and RT prediction’ enabled. For precursor ion generation, the maximum number of missed cleavages was set to 1, maximum number of variable modifications to 1 for Ox(M), peptide length range to 7-30, precursor charge range to 2-4, precursor m/z range to 380-980, and fragment m/z range to 150-2000. The quantification was set to ‘Robust LC (high precision)’ mode with normalization set to RT-dependent, MBR enabled, protein inferences set to ‘Genes’, and ‘Heuristic protein inference’ turned off.  MS1 and MS2 mass tolerances, along with the scan window size were automatically set by the software. Precursors were subsequently filtered at library precursor q-value (1%), library protein group q-value (1%), and posterior error probability (50%). Protein quantification was carried out using the MaxLFQ algorithm as implemented in the DIA-NN R package (https://github.com/vdemichev/diann-rpackage) and the number of peptides quantified in each protein group was counted as implemented in the DiannReportGenerator Package (https://github.com/URMC-MSRL/DiannReportGenerator).
